I will keep my land centered on the wheat-maize rotation because that is the most stable way for me to use my 7.0 mu, and I have well irrigation to support it. Since some family labor is off-farm, I will not make the plan too complicated or too labor-heavy. I will put 5.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 2.0 mu in cotton because it still gives me a way to spread risk across crops. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give enough nitrogen to support tillering and grain filling, and irrigate a few times because water is available and spring moisture can be unreliable here. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep fertilization stronger than wheat, and rely on 2 irrigations if rainfall is not enough. For cotton, I will stay moderate on fertilizer and water, because too much vegetative growth can create management trouble, and I want a practical plan I can handle with limited labor. I will use rotary tillage on the wheat-maize land for speed and convenience, and plough the cotton land once to give it a better seedbed. My goal is stable production, manageable field work, and lower risk rather than chasing the absolute highest yield.
